title: Certification Preparation

toc.text: What changed with the rename (know this cold)

html:
Everything prior has been the how. This phase is the prove it: the Salesforce Certified Data 360 Consultant exam (formerly Data Cloud Consultant). Here are the verified Spring '26 facts, the domain weights, and the study plan that maps this roadmap to the exam blueprint.

Learning Objectives

By the end of this phase, you will be able to:

  • Quote the verified exam facts (name, code, format, pricing) confidently.
  • Map the 6 domains to this roadmap's phases.
  • Run a domain-weighted study plan and take evidence-based mock examinations.
  • Know the exam-day/test-center behaviors (retake rules, prep resources).

1. Verified exam facts (Spring '26)

FactValue
Certification nameSalesforce Certified Data 360 Consultant (renamed from Data Cloud Consultant, effective Oct 14, 2025)
Exam codeData-Con-101
ReleaseSpring '26 (content updated with the Winter/Spring platforms)
Questions60 scored + up to 5 unscored (total up to 65)
Time105 minutes
Passing score70%
Cost (first attempt)$200 USD / ¥30,000 JPY
Retake$100 USD / ¥15,000 JPY
PrerequisiteNone
FormatMultiple-choice / multiple-select, mostly scenario-based
ResultImmediate Pass/Fail + score report
ValidityRequires maintenance for current-standing (release-based)

What changed with the rename (know this cold)

The Oct 14, 2025 change was brand-level: Data Cloud became Data 360, and the consultant credential followed. Question content on Data-Con-101 is continuously refreshed with platform releases (Winter/Spring '26), so the domain blueprint is stable but features (e.g. data graphs, real-time calculated insights, Agentforce grounding) advance. A candidate whose release notes stop at 2024 will fail in 2026.

2. Domain blueprint → this roadmap

WeightDomainWhere to study
14%Solution Positioning (data confusion/discovery, use cases)Phase 1, 17
13%Data 360 Setup and AdministrationPhase 1, 3, 11
18%Data Source Connection and IngestionPhases 2, 3
17%Harmonization and UnificationPhases 4, 5
18%Data Enhancements, Sharing, and AnalysisPhases 6, 12, 13
20%Data Activations and UtilizationPhases 7–10, 14

Priority signal: 20% on Activations/Utilization and 18% on Ingestion + 18% on Enhancements/Sharing/Analysis — almost 3/4 of the exam lives after ingestion but before reporting. The roadmap's ordering (identity → transforms → segments → activation → data actions → Agentforce) mirrors this exactly. Do not skip Phases 7–10 thinking "they are the last mile" — they are the heaviest weight.

3. Study plan (domain-weighted)

18 phases ≈ 10–12 weeks at ~8–10 h/week. Fix the bottom-heavy weights:

Week setFocusEvidence
1–2Phases 1–3 (positioning, setup, ingestion)Do all exercises + labs in 2, 3
3Phase 4 (identity resolution) + hands-onLab tests passing
4Phase 5 (transforms/calculated insights)SQL wins in labs
5Phase 6 (segmentation)Build 5 segments in exercise
6–7Phases 7–10 (activation/data actions)Activation audit + subscriber tests
8Phases 11–12 (consent, analytics)Governance + dashboard labs
9Phases 13–14 (AI, Agentforce)Prompts + data-graph exercises
10+Phase 15 mock exams + Phase 16 mini-projects2–3 full-domain mocks, score ≥ 75%

Evidence-based mock strategy

  1. Take a full-domain mock weekly in the last month; review why every wrong answer is wrong (the matter, it's exam-scenario).
  2. Average 75% on mocks for 3 consecutive weeks before booking.
  3. Focus review time by weight: a 20%-domain weakness is worth 5× a 14% one.

4. Case-study & scenario reading (the underrated technique)

Most Data-Con-101 questions are scenarios with a correct "which configuration/order of steps" answer. Train this exact skill:

  1. Identify the ask (activate? unify? who can see? which refresh?).
  2. Spot the constraint (consent, data space, retention, real-time vs batch).
  3. Choose the smallest correct configuration (consultants recommend the least complex viable answer).
  4. Re-read for traps: "marketing user", "without write-back", "real-time", "comply with GDPR".

Every phase's Certification Checkpoints and Self-Check blocks exist to build this reflex. The final 3 phases (16–18) are where you prove it on real-style problems.

5. Test-day & booking checklist

  • Register via Webassessor (Salesforce Trailmix "Certification" → Data 360 Consultant path) with the CRM/sf identity tied to your Dev Hub.
  • Check release window: candidates who re-certify on release changes must book the current-release exam.
  • 105 minutes is generous for 60 scorable Qs — budget ~1.5–2 min each; keep a buffer for the 1–2 long scenarios.
  • Retake window per policy: if you don't pass, schedule the retake at the reduced fee via the same Webassessor funnel.

Hands-On Exercises

Exercise 1: Blueprint map

Write one line under each of the 6 domains naming the 2 artifacts/phases you'd want fresh before the exam (e.g. "Heritage + Vector upload" under Source Connection; "data graph + activation" under Utilization).

Exercise 2: Fact card

Make a 20-question flashcard set from this roadmap (weights, prices, format, rename facts, retention/consent rules). Run it twice daily until you answer all from memory.

Exercise 3: Scenario battery

Write 6 scenario questions mixing (a) real-time chain broken (which hop?); (b) consent suppress; (c) data space scope; (d) on-the-fly vs materialize. Swap with a study buddy and grade each other's why.

Key Terms Glossary

TermDefinition
Data-Con-101The Data 360 Consultant exam code.
Data 360 ConsultantCurrent name of the consultant credential (formerly Data Cloud Consultant).
Passing score70%.
Scored vs unscored60 scored; up to 5 unscored pilot questions.
Domain weight% of the exam each blueprint domain carries.
MaintenanceRelease-based activities required to keep current-standing certification.
WebassessorThe registration portal for Salesforce certification exams.

Certification Checkpoints

  • I can recite the 5 exam facts (name, code, format, time, passing %, fees, retake) cold.
  • I know the rename (Data Cloud → Data 360) date and its exam implication.
  • I can map the 6 domains to roadmap phases and know the top-3 weights.
  • I maintain mock scores ≥ 75% for 3 consecutive weeks before booking.
  • I have booked my exam via Webassessor for the current release.

Self-Check

  1. Q: What is the current name of the credential and its exam code? — A: Salesforce Certified Data 360 Consultant (formerly Data Cloud Consultant); exam Data-Con-101.
  2. Q: 60 scored + up to 5 unscored, 105 minutes, 70%, $200/$100. — A: Correct facts — commit them; they appear in scenario-adjacent wording (e.g. "which cost applies", "how long do I have").
  3. Q: Which two domains are the heaviest? — A: Activations and Utilization (20%) and Enhancements, Sharing, and Analysis (18%) + Source Connection/Ingestion (18%) — study Phases 2–3 and 7–10 hardest.
